Purpose: Upstream is a vocabulary and checklist for designing a system of agents that turns tickets, pull requests and clocks into merged code on remote machines. Nothing of ours designs such a system; the autonomous-run playbook runs one local loop and takes only the brakes and task questions.

179. hook-gateway: Point the model base URL at a logging proxy for code-free capture of model calls only. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:15)
180. otlp-common-wire: Treat OpenTelemetry as the common transport, since harness and platform exports land in any OTLP backend. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:17)
181. tolerate-span-name-drift: Expect agent span names to drift while the conventions settle. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:17)
182. pick-no-platform: Use a deliberate none when runs are few, one human watches, and the question is only whether it failed and what it printed. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:23)
183. outgrow-none-signals: Move off none when search across runs, a per-run cost rollup, or longer retention is needed. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:23)
184. verify-runner-retention: Verify retention days per runner product. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:27)
185. pick-tracing-platform: Choose a tracing platform when the question is why the agent acted, across many runs, or token spend needs a per-run rollup. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:33)
186. self-host-for-transcripts: Self-host an open-source tracing platform to keep transcripts in-house. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:33)
187. budget-per-run-not-request: Budget tracing per run rather than per request, because agent runs are span-heavy. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:35)
188. verify-tracing-platform: Verify free-tier limits, billing unit, self-hosting tier and current ownership. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:39)
189. pick-general-apm: Choose an existing APM when the team already pays for it, runs must join app traces, or a monitor already reads from it. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:45)
190. nest-run-in-caller-trace: Propagate trace context so a run nests inside its caller's trace. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:45)
191. check-apm-volume-pricing: Weigh factory volume against the bill, since it is negligible on an existing APM and a surprise on a new one. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:47)
192. verify-apm-agent-view: Verify agent view status, harness setup guides and free-tier volumes. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:51)
193. pick-llm-gateway: Choose a gateway for per-run spend caps, one key vault, or a harness with no export of its own. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:57)
194. pair-gateway-with-tracing: Pair a gateway with a tracing or APM type to cover tool calls. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:57)
195. verify-gateway-maintained: Verify SaaS per-request pricing and whether the product is still actively developed. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:61)
196. obs-q-already-enough: Ask whether the runner or orchestrator already shows enough, and record a deliberate none if so. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:67)
197. obs-q-export-path: Ask which hooks the harness and product share, whether tool calls arrive as spans, and whether prompts need an opt-in. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:68)
198. obs-q-self-hosting: Ask about licence, tier and runtime for self-hosting. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:69)
199. obs-q-cost-estimate: Estimate per-run cost from one span per tool call, multiplied by runs per day. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:70)
200. obs-q-retention: Compare days kept on each tier with how far back the human looks. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:71)
201. obs-primary-sources: Take answers from pricing pages, harness integration docs, monitoring docs, the semantic conventions, repos and changelogs. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:73)
202. obs-staleness-order: Recheck the fast-changing facts first: limits, prices, beta flags, ownership, billing units, retention and span names. (OBSERVABILITY-PLATFORMS.md:75)

Suggested: wayfinder · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream scaffolds per-repository configuration (tracker, triage labels, domain-doc locations) that its other skills read. We have no setup skill: our skills read AGENTS.md and .repo-context/ directly, and we track with Beads.
Reason: Compared with domain-modeling because its domain-doc consumer rules are the only part with a counterpart; no skill of ours matches the setup purpose. Wayfinder shares four tracker-convention traits only because the tracker documents serve upstream's own wayfinder; ours keeps those on Beads. Suggested wayfinder by the computed signals only.

### Traits

- `tracker-config-doc` (new): absent; reject; reason: We track work only in Beads (AGENTS.md:118), so a per-repository tracker file has nothing to attach to; the owner rejected this skill whole on 2026-10-14 for the same reason (`2026-10-14-owner-review:004`).
- `triage-label-config` (new): absent; reject; reason: We track work only in Beads (AGENTS.md:118), so a label vocabulary file has nothing to attach to; the owner rejected this skill whole on 2026-10-14 for the same reason (`2026-10-14-owner-review:004`).
- `domain-docs-config` (new): absent; reject; reason: We declare those locations once, in AGENTS.md:102-103, and `domain-modeling` reads the declaration (`declared-glossary-location`); writing them into a second file would make two declarations that can drift.
- `draft-confirm-then-write` (new): absent; reject; reason: Nothing of ours scaffolds per-repository configuration for other skills: they read `AGENTS.md` and `.repo-context/` directly, so this setup step has no home.

- `one-question-at-a-time` (new): absent; reject; reason: Opposite stance where we interview: `grilling` and `brainstorming` batch the questions whose prerequisites are settled (`question-batching`), and nothing of ours runs a setup interview.
- `recommended-answer` (new): absent; reject; also in brainstorming (present), grilling (present); reason: No setup interview of ours to carry it; `grilling` and `brainstorming` already list this same trait for the interviews we run.
- `yes-accepts-recommendation` (new): absent; reject; also in brainstorming (variant), grilling (present); reason: No setup interview of ours to carry it; `grilling` already lists this same trait for the interviews we run.
